A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network training experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny Shakespeare, including sharpness trajectories, sensitivity studies, and quadratic-approximation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional Transformer learning-rate trajectories in Figures 2 and 4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects its stated Frank-Wolfe step from projecting the Hessian-vector product to explicitly maximizing its linearization over the norm ball. This is a limited correction to the sharpness-estimation procedure; the norm-specific gradient updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, its 5,000-example subset, and Tiny Shakespeare for the same image-classification and language-modeling tasks. The additional learning rates do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated optimizers and sharpness comparisons are retained. Figure 5's 'Muon without momentum' becomes 'normalized Spectral GD' with the same update and plotted results. Scion is newly cited but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Transformer loss changes from rescaled MSE in v1 Appendix G.1 to cross-entropy in v2 Appendix D; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing reruns. Figures 2 and 4 add learning rates 1e-5 and 0.015 respectively, and Figure 2 extends the trajectories. The infinity-norm restart-setting paragraph changes from {1,7,15} to {1,5,10}, matching the retained figure, although nearby prose still mentions 15.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 4 expand the Transformer learning-rate sweeps from two to three rates, adding limited evidence about the stability threshold's dependence on step size. The dedicated Frank-Wolfe, Polar Express, pre-stability oscillation, quadratic-approximation, and RMSprop analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds training-run replication counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Frank-Wolfe restarts remain controls of the sharpness-estimation algorithm, rather than statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 4 add Transformer trajectories for loss, gradient norm, directional smoothness, and generalized sharpness; Figure 2 also reports longer trajectories. The other plotted results, including all appendix figures, are retained. The reported loss revision prevents interpreting differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the directional-smoothness sign and Taylor remainder, distinguishes the unit-sphere definition from the unit-ball relaxation, and corrects Frank-Wolfe maximization derivations. Theorem 5.2 adds a valid dual-gradient selection and repairs negative-scaling handling in its proof; Theorem J.5 excludes zero initialization. These refine existing results while retaining their principal thresholds.

C1.justification: v2 narrows language about observations extending to all non-Euclidean methods to evidence across representative geometries. It also reframes the Muon connection around normalized spectral updates used within modern optimizers. The central geometry-dependent edge-of-stability contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly characterizes reported sharpness values as multi-restart Frank-Wolfe estimates and qualifies when a ball-constrained maximizer lies on the boundary. Its conclusion newly identifies stochastic, momentum, and adaptive extensions as open directions. Existing explanations of oscillations and the sharpness-threshold gap are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit description of full-batch Hessian-vector-product diagnostics, and the Transformer loss documentation is revised. Most of Appendix D's training information already appeared in v1 Appendix G.1, including five restarts, 50 Frank-Wolfe iterations, five Polar Express steps, and the implementation-source attribution.

R1.justification: v2 adds Boyd and Vandenberghe, Wu et al., Alimisis et al., and Pethick et al., connecting normalized spectral descent to Scion as well as Muon. It removes Hui and Belkin alongside the loss-description revision. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate versions of the same work.

P1.justification: The appendix is substantially reorganized: training details and experimental sections precede the proofs, with v1 Appendices D/E becoming v2 I/J and training details receiving a standalone section. The abstract, mechanism introduction, conclusion, and captions are also revised, and normalized-optimizer terminology is standardized.

P2.justification: The figure inventory is retained. Transformer rows in Figures 2 and 4 are redrawn with additional curves and revised axes or legends; captions are edited, Figure 6 moves, and appendix figures are redistributed. The spectral ResNet20/VGG11 caption also corrects its erroneous infinity-descent label.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical reliability by correcting Taylor/sign errors and the divergence proof's treatment of negative scaling. Narrower optimizer claims, clearer estimation qualifications, and appendix organization also help. Additional Transformer learning-rate checks provide limited support, while the generic-divergence gap and some restart-count inconsistencies remain unresolved.
